title: Russian drone strikes NATO territory in Romania — Putin blames Ukraine — 2026-05-30
narrative: On May 30, 2026, a Russian attack drone struck an apartment block in Galati, Romania — a NATO member state — punching through the concrete roof and causing a fire. A woman and her teenage son were hospitalized with burns. Romanian air force jets could not intercept because the drone was already over a built-up area. Putin claimed the drone was "likely Ukrainian." NATO says it is "ready to defend allied territory." Residents told the BBC: "They told us we are protected by NATO, not to worry. But look where we are now." Separately, a Ukrainian drone targeting northern Russia was recently knocked off course into Estonia and was shot down by a Romanian fighter jet as part of NATO's quick reaction force — proving the intercept capability exists when the political will is present.
telemetry: - Russian attack drone struck apartment block in Galati, Romania, early morning May 30, 2026
Drone punched through concrete roof, hit lift shaft which absorbed blast
Woman and teenage son hospitalized with bruises and minor burns
Romanian air force could not intercept — drone was over built-up area, too risky
Putin claimed the drone was "likely Ukrainian" (Al Jazeera, May 30)
NATO statement: "ready to defend allied territory against Russian attacks"
Contradiction: Romanian fighter jet DID shoot down a Ukrainian drone that strayed into Estonia (recent incident, same NATO quick reaction force)
Galati is on the Ukrainian border, a few miles away
analysis: The physical evidence is unambiguous: a Russian drone hit a NATO member's residential building. Putin's attribution to Ukraine is contradicted by the drone's flight path (from the Ukrainian border toward Romania, not the reverse) and by NATO's own recent interception of a Ukrainian drone in Estonian airspace using the same quick reaction force. The key OSINT angle: NATO CAN intercept drones over NATO territory — it proved this with the Estonian intercept — but CHOSE not to over Galati. The "too risky over built-up areas" explanation doesn't hold when the alternative is a drone hitting a residential building. This is a story about NATO's Article 5 threshold being tested and found wanting.
verdict: [SIPHONED VERDICT]: A Russian drone struck a NATO member's apartment building while Putin blamed Ukraine — and NATO, which recently proved it can intercept stray drones over allied territory, chose not to act.
